basisOfRecord.quote: To examine the patterns of ant diversity along elevational gradients, we conducted field surveys in the Qinling Mountains, a natural boundary between the warm temperate and subtropical zones in China.
We conducted this study in July 2021.

To collect epigaeic ants, we set up three pitfall traps (diameter: 65 mm; depth: 77 mm; volume: 160 ml) filled with conserving liquid (ethanol and ethylene glycol, 1:1, approximately 50 ml) and one paper trap (baited with tuna and honey) using a 297 mm × 420 mm white paper.

Following the methods outlined in the literature (Liu et al. 2016; Nooten et al. 2021), we constructed our ant community phylogenetic tree based on the phylogenetic tree with 269 ant genera worldwide from Economo et al. (2018).

measurementStatistic.quote: We measured six functional traits related to diet, habitat preference, and foraging strategy of ants.

Phylogenetic diversity was calculated using Faith’s PD (PD, the sum of the branch length of species within a community; Faith 1992) and mean pairwise distance (MPD, the mean distance between pairs of species in the phylogenetic tree within a community; Webb et al. 2002).
To generate an ant functional trait dendrogram, functional trait values were z-standardized and subsequently transformed into a Euclidean distance matrix.
We clustered ant species based on the Euclidean distance matrix using UPGMA and calculated FD_PD using the same method as PD (Petchey and Gaston 2006).
A total of 11,347 ant specimens were collected in the field, which belonged to 42 ant species, 27 genera and 4 subfamilies (Table S2).

At genus level (Fig. 2a and Table S5), the dominant species were from Crematogaster, Lasius, Formica, Nylanderia and Pheidole at 1000 m, respectively accounting for 21.88%, 16.88%, 15.62%, 10.72% and 10.12%.
